narration: We start at the left with Q_map, the stack of BEV query embeddings that drives the whole module. These queries fan out along two parallel branches.
The upper branch feeds the queries into the offset network theta_offset, which predicts a learned spatial offset for each query.
That offset is added to the reference points P_ref at the summation node, shifting each reference location to where the query actually wants to look.
The shifted points are used for sampling on the bird's-eye-view feature map F_bev, picking out the individual grid cells highlighted in color.
Sampling yields the sampled features: one feature vector gathered from F_bev per query and per offset location.
Back at the lower branch, the same queries also pass through a small MLP, which is the head that parameterises the sampling uncertainty.
The MLP outputs a mean mu_i and a variance sigma_i squared, defining a Gaussian used for dynamic resampling rather than a fixed weight.
Using the reparameterisation trick, alpha_i equals mu_i plus sigma_i times epsilon, giving stochastic attention weights that are sent up to the aggregation stage.
Aggregate combines the sampled features under those attention weights, a linear layer projects the result, and the output is the query update delta Q_map.
With the mask fully lifted, the complete pipeline is visible: queries produce offsets and uncertainties, sampling reads F_bev, and weighted aggregation returns the refined query residual.
